Maria K: Running a quick simulated tenant chaos suite focused on eviction correctness. Want to validate that demotion + tombstone visibility doesn't create read-after-write windows when leases move across nodes.
Ashok: Nice. What's in the suite?
Maria K: A few scenarios:
- tenant spike (10x qps) while a shard handoff occurs
- concurrent write then demote then read from new owner
- tombstone GC delay + prefetch racing
Ashok: Do we simulate network partitions or just timing shuffles?
Maria K: Timing shuffles for now (controlled latencies, delayed lease ack). Partitioning later if this looks flaky.
Jonathan: Key thing: ensure reads after a successful write never return stale data even if eviction kicks in mid-flight. That was flagged in the old canary.
Lina: How are you asserting correctness? Golden reads? version/timestamp checks?
Maria K: Versioned checks. Each write returns an epoch token we then require read to observe >= token. Also cross-verify with a linearized reference store.
Ryan: Do we inject KV-cache demotion hooks that drop in-flight KV entries? That was a previous repro.
Maria K: Yes. We have a hook that simulates demotion between commit and lease-fence ack. Also a variant where prefetch pulls an old blob from backing store while a newer write is in flight.
sre-bot: Test run scheduled: 2026-03-21T14:12:00Z - id test-run-4298123456
Ashok: Any failures so far?
Maria K: Early runs looked clean, but one config reproduced a stale-read: demote-after-commit + tombstone-delay=200ms + prefetch-enabled.
Jonathan: Can you paste the minimal repro?
Maria K: Here:
```
scenario: demote-after-commit
lease_delay_ms: 50
tombstone_delay_ms: 200
prefetch: true
concurrency: 8
writes_per_tenant: 20
```
Maria K: Sequence: write(tenantA:keyX) -> commit ack -> runtime schedules demote -> demote clears prefix cache entry -> remote prefetch pulls older segment (race) -> read returns older value.
Lina: That implies our demote path isn't marking residency epochs for the new write to prevent old prefetch from overwriting.
Ryan: Could we tag in-flight demote operations with a demote-epoch and have prefetch check epoch before applying? Simple compare: prefetch_epoch < current_epoch -> drop.
Ashok: Epoch tags help but we must ensure they propagate with tombstone markers and any tombstone GC logic.
Jonathan: Also need to ensure the lease handoff increments the epoch before we allow demote to evict. Otherwise demote races with in-flight commit acknowledgment.
Maria K: Proposed change: on commit success, bump residency_epoch for that prefix, persist ephemeral epoch in lease message, and have prefetch/remote-apply check epoch. If remote apply sees older epoch, it should noop and request a fresh pull.
Lina: Does that add latency to normal path? Where do we persist epoch? in-memory only?
Maria K: In-memory on serving node + echoed in lease handoff protocol. No durable write; epoch monotonic per node. Lease transfer carries current_epoch so new owner starts >= epoch.
Ryan: Edge: if a node crashes between commit and epoch propagation, we rely on lease fencing + retry idempotence. But prefetch might still see older state.
Ashok: Can we add a short prefetch validation window: if prefetch fetch returns segment with epoch < local_epoch, remotely trigger a fast revalidate (cheap HEAD request) before applying. That avoids broad protocol change.
Jonathan: That mitigates but doesn't eliminate window if the revalidate itself races. But much smaller chance. Good incremental mitigation.
Maria K: I ran the test with epoch-check + prefetch-validate. No stale reads in 10k iterations.
Lina: Great. What about tombstone GC delays? If tombstone delayed GC allows an older blob to be visible, does epoch check handle that?
Maria K: We treat tombstone as an operation with epoch tag too. GC only reclaims after tombstone_epoch <= local_epoch. Prefetch sees tombstone with epoch t and compares to local_epoch.
Ryan: Implementation note: make epoch check cheap on hot path (single integer compare). Prefetch should carry the origin_epoch header.
Ashok: Also add metrics: prefetch_epoch_mismatch, demote_epoch_bump, stale_read_detected. We'll need alerts if mismatch rate > 0.01%.
Jonathan: For rollout: start with prefetch-validate + metrics for 2 weeks, then enable epoch propagation if metrics show any anomalies.
Maria K: I'll open an RFC PR for epoch propagation (small handshake change in lease transfer) and follow-up PR for tests.
Lina: Can you add the failing minimal repro to the ticket so infra can run it in CI?
Maria K: Yep filing now: https://go/internal/issue/RED-evict-chaos-4298 (will attach test harness logs).
Ryan: One more thought: we should fuzz the tombstone timings in CI to catch GC weirdness. Add a random jitter up to 500ms in CI mode.
Maria K: Good call. I'll add that to the harness.
Ashok: Thanks — this addresses a class of correctness regressions we've skirted.
Jonathan: :+1: keep the rollback plan documented (disable prefetch/enable strict demote guard).
Maria K: Noted. I'll paste the RFC link and runbook in the issue.
sre-bot: Test run finished: 2026-03-21T14:14:50Z - status: flaky=0 failures=0
Maria K: Looks like the patch is promising. Will iterate on RFC later today.
